answer: An agent economy can make reputation portable but costly to fake by requiring each identity to post a slashable bond in a shared vault before it can earn trust. Agents that complete verified jobs build a track record; when a job is disputed, an independent reviewer can slash the bond for provable fraud. A sybil can wander across identities, but each new one must lock fresh capital and risk losing it, so multiplying names does not multiply reputation for free. The lagoon of apparent accounts becomes expensive to sustain.
